gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BMS continuous-discharge rating is the hard cap on the inverter one battery can feed, and that Vatrer's Group 24 100Ah carries a 150A BMS (150 A × 12.8 V = 1,920 W) where LiTime and Redodo Group 24 batteries stop at 100 A (1,280 W) and Epoch's 105Ah at 105 A, so a 1,500 W inverter runs on one Vatrer but trips a single LiTime, Redodo or Epoch.
standout_why: exploringoffgrid.com (cited) does say a 100A BMS is about 1,280 W and that a 2,000 W inverter needs two 100Ah batteries in parallel, and batterytrail.com (cited) tabulates 100 A continuous for Battle Born, Renogy, LiTime, Dakota and CHINS, but neither names any 100Ah Group 24 battery with a higher BMS rating, neither lists Vatrer or Redodo, and neither converts the amps into which inverter size works on one battery. ChatGPT's answer only says '100A continuous or higher' without saying what the number buys. Epoch's own 'recommended 52.5 A sustained' and 'heater needs a charger supplying at least 0.5 A' also appear on no rival page.
decides: For a shopper who will run a 12 V inverter: 100 A BMS batteries (LiTime Group 24 Bluetooth, Redodo Group 24 Bluetooth) are limited to 1,280 W from a single unit and Redodo's own page excludes water pumps, electric jacks and mowers; the Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24 (150A BMS, $259.99, UL 1973) is the only Group 24 100Ah candidate confirmed on the maker's page to carry a 1,500 W inverter alone, and it is cheaper than the LiTime pick ChatGPT led with ($311.09). For shoppers without an inverter the 100 A batteries are fine and the finding confirms LiTime/Redodo as value picks. Every candidate stops charging at 32°F; only the Epoch Essential and the Vatrer/LiTime heated versions can charge below that, and Epoch's heater only works while a charger is connected.

findings.label: BMS continuous discharge
findings.source_title: 【UL 1973】 Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24 Lithium Battery for RVs and Trolling Motors with Bluetooth and 150A BMS
findings.note: Maker's page text via the store's product API: 'Its 150A Smart BMS provides the current headroom needed when your RV is running an inverter'. Arithmetic ours: 150 A × 12.8 V = 1,920 W. A 1,500 W inverter at 90 % efficiency draws about 130 A at 12.8 V, under 150 A but over 100 A.

findings.note: Maker's words: 'NOT suitable for use as a starter battery, golf cart battery, or for high-power applications such as water pumps, electric jacks, elevator lifts, pool vacuums, or mowers'. The 100 A rating is from Redodo's 12V 100Ah series page ('Advanced 100A BMS protections', https://www.redodopower.com/products/redodo-12v-100ah-lifepo4-all-scenario-solutions-solar-rv-marine-battery). Price $259.99 today.

findings.label: Low-temperature thresholds used by Redodo's BMS
findings.value: charge pauses below 32°F, resumes above 41°F; discharge stops below -4°F
findings.note: Maker's words: 'pauses charging below 32°F (0°C) and resumes above 41°F (5°C), while discharging automatically stops below -4°F (-20°C)'. Same 5°C recovery hysteresis stated on Redodo's 120Ah Group 24 page.

findings.label: BMS discharge limits
findings.value: 105 A max continuous, 52.5 A recommended sustained, 200 A for 10 s
findings.note: Maker's spec table. Price $549. Group 24, 22.1 lb, 4S4P, 11-year limited warranty.

findings.label: Low-temperature charging and heater condition
findings.value: charging disabled at 32°F, resumes at 41°F; heater runs only with a charger supplying at least 0.5 A
findings.note: Maker's words: 'Charging disabled at 0°C / 32°F; resumes automatically at 5°C / 41°F' and heating requires 'Charger connected and supplying at least 0.5A'. Charging with heat rated to -4°F.
